t: Introduction: types of examination of living persons
n: In this topic we shall consider the types of examination of living persons. Examination of living persons is the type of examination most often carried out in practice. It is ordered in criminal, civil and administrative cases. The examination is carried out in the outpatient department and in district, city and inter-district departments; in some cases also in a medical institution. There are four types: bodily injuries, in which the nature of the injury and the degree of severity are determined; sexual conditions, that is, sex, virginity, pregnancy and others; sexual crimes, that is, rape, sodomy and lewd acts; and health and age, in which simulation and artificial disease are investigated.

t: Examination of sexual conditions: what is established
n: Let us consider what is established in the examination of sexual conditions. Such an examination is needed both in investigating criminal cases and in hearing civil cases. In it, sex, sexual maturity, virginity, reproductive ability, pregnancy, delivery and abortion are determined. The question of pregnancy arises in cases of infanticide, child abduction, criminal abortion and rape. Thus sexual conditions are studied in five directions: sex, maturity and virginity, reproductive ability, pregnancy, and delivery and abortion.

t: Determination of sex: when and why it is needed
n: Let us consider when and why sex needs to be determined. The need to determine true sex arises when sex has been wrongly established, when issuing an identity document, or on entering a special educational establishment. An examination is also carried out in annulment of marriage, recovery of maintenance and investigation of sexual crimes, if there is doubt about the registered sex of the person. Normally the external sexual features form in accordance with the existing sex gland, that is, ovary or testis. If a defect arises in the embryonic period, the external genitalia may not fully correspond to a particular sex; hence examination is necessary.

Hermaphroditism is the simultaneous presence of genital organs characteristic of two sexes. Its true and false forms are distinguished. True hermaphroditism is very rare; in it there are male and female sex glands, and signs of spermatogenesis and oogenesis are found together. Attention: in practice the false form is commoner. In it the gland belongs to one sex and the external features to the other. In the false male there is a testis, that is, spermatogenesis, the features resemble female ones, and a small penis and cryptorchidism occur. In the false female there is an ovary, that is, oogenesis, and the features resemble male ones.

Determination of true sex proceeds in stages. The first stage is history: medical documents are studied, and menstruation, nocturnal emissions, sexual drive and specialists' documents are taken into account. The second stage is anthropometry, that is, measurements. In the third stage the external and secondary features are examined. The fourth stage is clinical and laboratory examination: the function of the sex gland is determined by clinical, laboratory and functional investigations. The fifth stage is chromosome analysis: examination of chromosomes in leucocytes may show genetic sex.

We consolidate the topic with quick questions. Question 1: what sex glands are present in true hermaphroditism? Answer: both male and female sex glands. Question 2: which gland functions in false male hermaphroditism? Answer: the testis, that is, spermatogenesis; the external features resemble female ones. Question 3: and in false female hermaphroditism? Answer: the ovary, that is, oogenesis; the external features resemble male ones. Question 4: how is genetic sex determined? Answer: by examining chromosomes in the leucocytes of the blood.

The concept of sexual maturity. Sexual maturity means this: the body is developed so that a sexual life can be led without harm to health and further growth. In women it covers sexual intercourse, pregnancy, carrying the fetus, delivery and breastfeeding, in men the ability for intercourse and fertilisation. Those under 14 years are considered sexually immature. The question of maturity arises in the period from 14 years to marriageable age. Its practical significance has now decreased: in the Criminal Code liability is tied to age, that is, Articles 118 and 119 to 18 and 14 years, Articles 128 and 129 to 16 years.

t: Indicators of sexual maturity in girls
n: Indicators of sexual maturity in girls are given as minimum limits. Body length standing 150 cm, sitting 80 cm. Chest circumference 78-80 cm. Of the pelvic dimensions, the distance between the iliac spines is 26-27 cm, between the femoral trochanters 29 cm, and the external conjugate 17-18 cm. An important remark: the indicators are relative. Sometimes women with smaller dimensions also give birth without harm to the body. In girls under 14, because of acceleration, that is, accelerated development, larger values may be found. Usually by 16-17 years the development of the pelvis allows a normal course of delivery.

t: Criteria of intercourse, ovulation and the uterus
n: Let us consider the criteria of intercourse, ovulation and the uterus. The ability for sexual intercourse depends on sufficient development of the external genitalia, in particular the vagina. After ovulation pregnancy is possible; ovulation is related to a properly formed menstrual cycle. At maturity the body of the uterus makes up 2/3 of its length and the cervix 1/3. Otherwise the fetus is not carried for the due term. In boys maturity is determined less often; here, together with a urologist or andrologist, general development, genital organs, secondary features and gland function are studied.

Case analysis. Situation: an examination to determine sexual maturity has been ordered for a girl aged between 14 years and marriageable age. It is carried out with the participation of an obstetrician-gynaecologist. In assessment, physical development, the external and internal genital organs, secondary features, pelvic dimensions and menstruation are taken into account together. Attention: dimensions have relative significance. A woman with smaller values can also bear a child; before 14 years acceleration gives larger values. Question: can one conclude from height alone that the girl is mature or immature? Why?

t: Virginity and the structure of the hymen
n: Virginity, that is, virginitas, is determined mainly by the anatomical integrity of the hymen. The hymen is a fold of the vaginal mucosa containing connective and muscle fibres, vessels and nerves. In the hymen the base, free edge and opening are distinguished. There may be several openings, or none at all. In describing the hymen, comparison with a clock face is used. In virginity, if a fingertip is introduced carefully into the opening, a contractile ring is felt.

Forms of the hymen. Nikitin and Serdyukov divided hymens by structure into three groups. Group 1 is common: annular, semilunar and funnel-shaped. Group 2 is uncommon: lobed, spiral and fringed. Group 3 is very rare: two-windowed, septate and imperforate hymen. In unusual forms the free edges of the hymen are uneven. In figure 12.1 of the textbook the annular, semilunar, fringed and septate forms are shown.

On deflowering. Disruption of the anatomical integrity of the hymen at first intercourse, that is, deflowering, leads to loss of virginity. Under the action of the glans of the penis a complete or incomplete tear forms in the hymen. A complete tear reaches the base of the hymen, an incomplete one does not. Sometimes deflowering does not occur in intercourse; this is seen mainly in elastic, stretchable, low hymens with many natural notches. Attention: the integrity of the hymen may be disrupted also by a finger, various objects or a surgical operation. Injury of the hymen is not always from sexual intercourse.

t: Stages of healing of a hymenal tear
n: Let us consider the stages of healing of a hymenal tear. The age can be determined only in the first weeks. After three weeks this question cannot be resolved. At first there are bleeding and swelling. Then a whitish coating appears at the edges. By the end of week 1 granulation, within 2-3 weeks a scar forms. After 3 weeks the time is indeterminable. A tear of a thin elastic hymen heals considerably faster than that of a thick fleshy one. Healing depends on the size of the injury, the features of the organism, and the shape and structure of the hymen.

t: Distinguishing a tear from a natural notch
n: Distinguishing a tear from a natural notch. The state of the edges of a tear depends on its age. The edges of an old tear are comparatively thick and scarred. A tear is more often in the lower segment, between 5 and 7 o'clock, and a complete tear reaches the base. A natural notch, however, occurs in various segments, mostly does not reach the base, and its edges do not differ from other areas. Attention: a natural notch and a tear are not the same. Distinguishing them often becomes necessary. If virginity is in doubt, a forensic medical expert is consulted as soon as possible.

Signs confirming sexual intercourse. Intercourse is confirmed by finding semen in the vagina, development of pregnancy and infection with venereal diseases. Semen usually persists in the vagina for up to 3-5 days. Therefore the sooner the sample is taken, the more reliable the laboratory result. In examination in a rape case, a vaginal swab and imprints from the pubis, perineum and thighs are taken as quickly as possible. With time the probability of finding spermatozoa decreases. Attention, there is a risk of error: disruption of the integrity of the hymen does not always mean sexual intercourse.

Case analysis: virginity. Situation: a girl was brought for examination. In the lower part of the hymen, on the clock face between 5 and 7, a tear reaching the base was found. Question: is this a tear or a natural notch? A natural notch may be in various segments of the hymen. A tear is more often in the lower segments, between 5 and 7. The edges of an old tear are comparatively thick and scarred. By time: at the end of week 2 - in week 3 a scar forms on the edge of the tear. The age of the disruption of integrity is determined only in the first weeks, after three weeks it is impossible.

Reproductive ability. In a man it is sexual intercourse and fertilisation; in a woman the possibility of intercourse, pregnancy and delivery. Fertilising ability is determined by laboratory examination of the ejaculate. If motile spermatozoa are found, the ability is confirmed. In a man the hindrances are: impotence, in which the CNS, a defect, an endocrine disease, neurosis; also azoospermia, necrospermia, asthenospermia. In a woman: atresia of the vagina, scar, tumour, vaginismus; atresia of the uterus and tubes, age; narrow pelvis and deformity of the pelvis. The examination is carried out with the participation of clinician-specialists; sometimes examination in hospital.

Let us consider the conditions that hinder conception and delivery. The ability to conceive is excluded by conditions related to age, that is, sexual immaturity or menopause. Also excluding are diseases of the genital organs, that is, inflammation, tuberculosis, gonorrhoea, malformations, that is, atresia of the uterus and tubes, and tumours. Chronic infection, intoxications and previous operations, that is, amputation of the uterus, ovary or tube, also remove the ability. A narrow pelvis, deformity of the pelvic bones, and consequences of diseases of the genital organs, that is, tumour and scar, hinder natural delivery.

t: Signs for determining an ongoing pregnancy
n: Signs for determining an ongoing pregnancy. In pregnancy there are no periods. But do not forget that sometimes a pregnant woman has bloody discharge, and some diseases run with menopause. The mammary glands enlarge; the nipple and areola enlarge and become pigmented. These signs are clearly visible from month 2. In the laboratory chorionic gonadotropin is determined; it is produced from the earliest period. The size, shape and consistency of the uterus change. Reliable signs: on auscultation the fetal heartbeat, on palpation and ultrasound the parts of the fetal body and movement. The term is determined as in obstetrics. In the second half the abdomen enlarges, whitish lines, that is, striae gravidarum, and pigmentation in the midline appear.

Let us recall the signs of an ongoing pregnancy by groups. Probable signs: cessation of periods and changes in the mammary glands, clear from month 2. Sometimes bloody discharge or diseases running with menopause must be taken into account. Laboratory sign: chorionic gonadotropin. Signs of the uterus and abdomen: the size, shape and consistency of the uterus change; in the second half the abdomen enlarges, whitish vertical lines, that is, striae gravidarum, and pigmentation in the midline appear. Reliable signs: the fetal heartbeat, and the parts and movement of the fetus.

Determining a previous delivery. In the first days the breasts are swollen, the areola darker, and there is discharge. The perineum is wide, the vaginal introitus open, and the vaginal walls somewhat prolapsed. In delivery the hymen is damaged; in its place separate flaps with haemorrhages remain, that is, carunculae myrtiformes. In a woman who has given birth the external os of the cervix is slit-like, in one who has not usually round. In the first days it is not difficult to determine the time of delivery.

Types of abortion. Abortion is termination of pregnancy before 22 weeks. It may be spontaneous or artificial. Artificial abortion is divided into medical, that is, artificial, and criminal; the difference lies in the performer and the conditions. Medical abortion is performed by an obstetrician-gynaecologist, takes place in a medical institution in compliance with the rules, and has preliminary examination and subsequent follow-up. Criminal abortion is performed by an untrained worker or an uninformed person, in an institution or outside it. The Criminal Code, Article 114, determines liability for criminal abortion.

t: Methods and consequences of criminal abortion
n: Methods and consequences of criminal abortion. Criminal abortion is carried out by untrained persons. Article 114 of the Criminal Code determines liability. The method determines the marks on the body. In the mechanical method an instrument, object or pressurised liquid is used, and the marks are abrasions, bruises and wounds. In the chemical method a drug, acid, alkali or alcohol is used, with poisoning and chemical burn as the consequence. In the thermal method hot water or a hot bath is used, and the mark is a thermal burn. Electric current is used very rarely. Dangerous complications: air embolism, shock, haemorrhage, perforation, poisoning and infection.

Case analysis: pregnancy and abortion. A training situation: in a woman a pregnancy has been terminated, and there is suspicion that the abortion was performed outside a medical institution. Suppose that on examination abrasions, bruises, wounds and haemorrhages into the mucosa are found in the vagina and uterus. Question 1: for which method are these marks characteristic? How does the examination determine pregnancy, termination and method? Question 2: what life-threatening complications may be expected in the woman, for example embolism, shock, perforation?

t: Sexual crimes and articles of the Criminal Code
n: Sexual crimes and articles of the Criminal Code. Article 118 is rape, a crime against sexual freedom. Article 119 is unnatural intercourse, also against sexual freedom. Article 120 is sodomy, without violence. Article 129 is lewd acts, up to 16 years, a crime against the family, youth and morality. Also Article 113: knowing transmission of a venereal disease or HIV, that is, human immunodeficiency virus. In sodomy both participants are liable. If there was violence, only the active participant is liable under Article 119. Attention: 118 and 120 are not the same. In rape there is violence, in sodomy there is not.

Procedure of examination in rape. Article 118: sexual intercourse against the victim's will with violence, threat or by taking advantage of helplessness. Before the examination, the order appointing the examination, the record of examination of the scene and the medical documents are studied. Then the victim is interviewed. A gynaecological history is collected: age at menarche, last menstruation, onset of sexual life, last sexual intercourse, pregnancies, deliveries and abortions. Attention: rape is a legal concept. The expert looks for objective signs confirming intercourse or attempt, violence and helplessness. In theory men may also be victims, in practice mainly women.

Injuries and marks in rape. In violence, bruises and abrasions are inflicted by the offender's hands and feet: the inner surface of the thigh, the genitalia, sometimes the breast and neck, which are bites. Tear of the hymen is found, and sometimes haemorrhage and tear of the vaginal wall and perineum. Finding semen in the vagina, on the pubis, in the perineum and on the thigh is important evidence. Besides semen, there may be traces of hair and blood. Swabs and imprints are taken as quickly as possible after the event: as time passes the probability of finding spermatozoa decreases. Attention: injury of the vagina and perineum occurs also in a woman who leads a sexual life.

t: Examination of the suspect and unnatural intercourse (Article 119)
n: Examination of the suspect and unnatural intercourse. Article 119: sexual intercourse through the mouth or anus with violence, threat or by taking advantage of helplessness, that is, satisfaction of need in an unnatural way. In the victim, the presence of injury or change in the oral cavity and around it, the anus and around it, and the lower part of the rectum is checked. The suspect is also examined. If traces of blood or hair belonging to the woman are found on the penis and pubis, they are taken for laboratory examination. On various parts of the body, including the external genitalia, as a result of the victim's struggle there may be bruises, abrasions and bite marks.

Quick questions. Question 1: which marks show that violence was used? Answer: mainly bruises and abrasions, often on the inner surface of the thigh and in the region of the genitalia. Question 2: why does a threat leave no marks? Answer: a threat leaves no objective signs on the victim. Other medico-biological signs are therefore studied. Question 3: why should the sample be taken quickly? As time passes the probability of finding spermatozoa decreases. A swab is taken from the vagina, an imprint from the external regions. Attention: injury of the vagina and perineum occurs also in women who lead a sexual life. This sign by itself does not prove violence.

Sodomy: active and passive participants. Article 120: satisfaction by a man of sexual need with a man without violence, that is, male homosexuality. Both the active and the passive participant are subjects of the crime, and both are brought to liability. If violence, threat or helplessness was used, only the active person is liable under Article 119; the passive person is the victim. In the active participant the penis and pubic region are examined, and blood, hair, faeces and an oily substance are sought; traces persist in the coronal sulcus. In the passive participant the anus, rectum and perineum are examined, and semen, hair and an oily substance are sought; abrasions, haemorrhages and fissures are found, and the folds are smoothed.

Preventing errors in sodomy. Diseases running with constipation or diarrhoea, proctitis, paraproctitis, haemorrhoids and rectal prolapse may be wrongly interpreted. Residual marks of surgical interventions in this area may also be wrongly assessed as a sign of passive sodomy. In the interview of the passive participant attention is paid to these questions. If necessary, a proctologist's consultation is obtained within the examination. Attention: a sign of disease is not a sign of passive sodomy. With few acts of intercourse, in an adult passive participant no injury may be found at all.

Lewd acts are shameless, corrupting acts of a sexual nature committed against a person under sixteen years. Examples: touching a genital organ with the hand or penis and rubbing, undressing in front of a child, masturbation, showing pornographic images and films. This crime belongs to the group of crimes against the family, youth and morality. Liability is set out in Article 129 of the Criminal Code. Possible marks: reddening, abrasions, bruises, haemorrhage in the vagina, incomplete tear of the hymen, traces of semen. Attention: sometimes no marks remain.

Marks and samples in lewd acts. Injuries: in the genital region reddening, abrasions and bruises may appear. In girls there may be haemorrhage in the vaginal mucosa, a superficial tear, haemorrhage in the hymen and an incomplete tear. Marks: in girls, traces of semen are found on the external genitalia and thighs, sometimes on clothing; swabs and imprints are taken to the laboratory. Sometimes lewd acts leave no marks at all on the victim.

Venereal diseases, spread of HIV and AIDS. Article 113: knowingly infecting, or putting at risk of infection, with a venereal disease or HIV, that is, human immunodeficiency virus, or AIDS, is a crime. These crimes belong to the group of crimes dangerous to life or health. Attention: rape and sodomy are crimes against sexual freedom. The examination is carried out with the participation of a dermatovenereologist and AIDS specialists: the suspect and victim undergo examination and laboratory investigation, and documents are analysed. The stage of the course of the disease is taken into account: a person found to be at a late stage is a subject of the crime. A medical worker who improperly performed his duties may also be liable.

Case analysis: sexual crimes. Situation: a woman was brought for examination with suspected rape. On examination there may be bruises and abrasions on the inner surface of the thigh and in the region of the genitalia, and a tear in the hymen. A threat, however, leaves no objective marks. A vaginal swab and imprints from the pubis, perineum and thigh are taken as quickly as possible after the event. With time the probability of finding spermatozoa decreases. The suspect is also examined: bruises, abrasions, bites, and traces of blood and hair belonging to the woman on the penis and pubis are sought. Question: which samples are taken? First the order, record and medical documents are studied, then the interview and collection of the gynaecological history are carried out.

Algorithm of conducting the examination. The examination of living persons is carried out by a general six-stage algorithm. The first and second stages: the circumstances of the case and the medical documents. The circumstances of the case are first studied from the data of the order or ruling appointing the examination. The originals of medical documents are provided; the person who ordered the examination answers for their authenticity. The third stage is the interview of the person, the fourth the examination of the person, the fifth special investigations, the sixth the expert's conclusion.

Conditions of examination and participants. Identity is confirmed by passport, military ID or birth certificate. If there is no document, identity may also be confirmed by the person who ordered the examination. In the examination of sexual conditions and crimes, besides the identity document, two photographs of the person examined are provided. In examination of a person of the other sex and exposure of the body, the investigator leaves. Examination of a patient under treatment, if health permits, is carried out with the participation of the person who ordered it and the treating doctor or head of department; it is entered in the case history. Minors are examined in the presence of parents or a teacher, persons lacking capacity in the presence of a legal representative.

The main theses of the topic. Examination of sexual conditions is ordered to determine sex, sexual maturity, virginity, reproductive ability, pregnancy, delivery and abortion. The age of disruption of the integrity of the hymen is determined only in the first weeks; after three weeks this question cannot be resolved. In rape, injuries and traces of semen, blood and hair are sought. Swabs and imprints are taken as quickly as possible, since over time the reliability of the result decreases. The whole examination of living persons is carried out by a six-stage algorithm: from the circumstances of the case to the expert's conclusion.
